On this page

Overview ​

Saidi is a hosted AI orchestrator you talk to like a team leader. You give it a brief; it turns that brief into a plan, hands each task to an agent that is scoped to the right repo or the right specialty, checks the result against criteria written before the work started, and reports back with a branch you can review.

It is not a chat window with a code interpreter bolted on. The unit of work is a Run — a durable, resumable thread that survives a server restart, keeps one shared context across every agent that participates, and accumulates its commits on one branch instead of cutting a fresh one every time.

The cast ​

ActorWhat it is
You (the operator)The only human in the loop. You brief, approve, and decide.
PRIMEThe orchestrating agent. It plans, delegates, relays questions, and summarises. You only ever talk to PRIME.
Project agentsRepo-scoped agents. One per registered project, working in that repo's checkout, on that repo's branch.
Custom agentsNon-repo specialists (Finance, Research, Ops…) grouped into departments, each with an optional lead that routes work to its team.

The loop ​

  1. Brief — you describe the objective in chat, or start a Run directly.
  2. Plan — PRIME freezes a checklist. Every task carries acceptance criteria that a verifier could actually rule on ("npm test passes", "dist/report.pdf exists"), not quality adjectives.
  3. Delegate — PRIME calls delegate_to_project or run_agent. In guided mode the engine itself owns the dispatch loop: it picks ready tasks, batches independent ones, and advances only on a passed verdict.
  4. Verify — mechanical checks run first (a shell command judged by its exit code), then an independent model verifier if needed. Evidence is collected by the engine off git — the branch, the base, the commits, the files changed.
  5. Report — PRIME summarises. The Run holds the whole thread, the per-call usage ledger, and an append-only verification log that no plan amendment can erase.

What makes it different ​

Verified, not asserted A task's done is a verdict from something other than the agent that did the work. Failing checks are trusted from any source; passing checks are only trusted from a source the Run did not author — because the plan author writes both the criteria and the checks, and naming a criterion is not proving it. Verification Your workspace is the boundary Agents, runs, memory, connections and the credit ledger all belong to one workspace and never cross into another. Runs and chats belong to whoever created them — no role reads another member's work unless it is shared. Config lives in your repos; memory lives in Saidi and is never committed to a client repo. Tenancy & identity Approval is a real gate A project's policy decides whether writes need your explicit confirmation, whether work goes on a new saidi/* branch or the current one, and what command proves it worked. Project policy

Verification is only as good as the criterion

A criterion like "the code is clean" cannot be checked by anything. A criterion like "npm test exits 0" can. The quality of a Run is decided when the plan is written, not when the agent starts typing — see Plans & Tasks.
